CHIEF COMPLAINT
Left ankle pain after injury.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient reports he stepped off a curb while on a walk with his wife yesterday and landed on his left ankle incorrectly. He denies hearing a pop but describes the ankle feeling extended and stretched. Pain is localized to the outside of the ankle and has been present for a couple of days. He was able to walk back to the house after the incident but reports it was painful. He rates his pain as 8/10 without medication and 7/10 with ibuprofen or acetaminophen. He has been managing the injury with ibuprofen, elevation, ice, and keeping weight off the ankle.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Patient reports no substantial prior injuries to the left ankle.

MEDICATIONS
Ibuprofen - taken for ankle pain.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works from home and takes regular walks with his wife.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vitals stable but slightly elevated. Focused exam of left ankle reveals ecchymosis and swelling over the lateral malleolus with edema. Tenderness to palpation on the lateral side with soft tissue swelling. No laxity appreciated in the joint. No bony tenderness to palpation of the foot. Neurovascular exam intact: capillary refill brisk (less than 3 seconds), strong dorsalis pedis pulses bilaterally, motor and sensation intact and symmetric bilaterally.

RESULTS
X-ray of left ankle shows no fracture or bony abnormalities.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Left ankle sprain of the lateral ligament complex. Continue RICE protocol (rest, ice, elevation, compression). Patient will be provided an air cast for ankle stabilization and crutches. Patient to stay off the leg but start walking as tolerated. Continue NSAIDs to reduce pain and swelling. Follow-up appointment in 2 weeks. Patient instructed to return if experiencing significant pain or if symptoms worsen.
